list.name: Kaze
list.text: The road east. Every year the festival lanterns come down this way and float off at the Crossing.

list.name: Mio
list.text: The trees are talking. Not words. More like… someone humming with their mouth closed.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: That’s the Forest. It hums the names of everyone who walked through it. Most of the names are getting quiet.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: There’s an old stump north of the path. My grandmother said a fox spirit taught her a trick there. I want to show you.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: Here. Watch the leaf on the stump. Shift, and it’s on the Far Shore. Shift back, and it’s gone again, right?

list.name: Kaze
list.text: Now hold the Lantern still. Don’t push it toward either shore. Just… tell the light to stay.
The leaf stays. One Far Shore leaf, resting on a Near Shore stump, glowing faintly.

list.name: Mio
list.text: It’s still here. I anchored it.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: That’s the trick. An Anchor holds one Shore’s picture in place for a little while. Statues, bridges, doorsteps. Things that need both Shores at once.

Mio learned ANCHOR. In battle it locks the current Shore for 3 turns. In the field (Menu → Skills → Anchor, 6 SP + 8 Lumen) it holds a Shore’s image in place: use it next to statues, drifting bridges and doorsteps.

An old stump.

then.text: A single glowing leaf rests on it, from both Shores at once.
The statue keeps its anchored note. Somewhere on the other Shore, a partner waits.

else.text: A round stone statue with a hollow throat. It seems to be waiting to be sung to.

br.text: Mio hums. The statue answers with one clear note… which starts to fade.

then.text: Both statues sing the same note, one on each Shore. The roots across the north path loosen and draw back like sleepy fingers.

then.name: Mio
then.text: They were singing to each other the whole time. They just couldn’t hear.

then.name: Kaze
then.text: North, then. The mist past the roots is the Grove. If anyone knows how to cross a river that forgets, it’s someone in there.

then.name: Mio
then.text: If I Shift, the note will stop. Unless I anchor it.
The Anchor wraps the note in light. It keeps ringing, even when the Shore turns.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: Two statues, but I can only see one. Shift, and I see the other.

list.name: Mio
list.text: They have to sing together. One Shore at a time won’t work…
Thick roots knot across the path. They tremble whenever the statues hum.

list.name: Rustle Sprite
list.text: Shh-shh. Rustle-rustle. You smell of lanterns. Lantern people always want things.

list.name: Rustle Sprite
list.text: I have a cord of knotted names. Someone dropped it at the Crossing a hundred autumns ago. Tie it to a Hollowed one and their name comes back.

br.name: Rustle Sprite
br.text: Ohhh. Flowers that remember the sun. Here, here. Mind the knots.

br.name: Kaze
br.text: There was a pilgrim at the Crossing, Mio. A grey one. He just stood there.

else.name: Rustle Sprite
else.text: Bring me flowers. A whole bundle. The Mist Peddler in the Grove sells them, or a Marigold Moth might drop some.

list.name: Rustle Sprite
list.text: Rustle-rustle. Tie it gently. Names bruise.
On the Far Shore, the humming is clearer. It is a list of names, sung very softly. Mio hears Sachi’s, and her grandfather’s.

list.name: Mio
list.text: Kaze… it skipped one. It went from my grandfather straight to me.

list.name: Kaze
list.text: My mother. The Forest forgot her, too. That’s what the Hollow does. It starts with the names.
Oto’s bell jingles by itself. There is something tucked under the roots.
Empty. The bell is quiet now.

The chest is empty.
The chest is empty.

lines: A thread of light leads into the ferns. A young man, laughing, ties a cord around his little sister’s wrist so she won’t get lost at the festival.
“Yoshi,” she calls him. The name hangs in the air like a firefly.

then.text: The cord at Mio’s wrist pulls gently east, toward the Crossing.

else.text: The thread of light dims, then points somewhere else.
